About

Sports Cards Near Me is an independent Canadian card-shop directory built and maintained by Nathan Wiebe, a CPA who buys and sells cards himself. It lists 614 shops across 179 cities in 11 provinces and territories, compiled from public sources, reviewed by a person, and rebuilt daily.

Who runs this

My name is Nathan Wiebe. I'm a Chartered Professional Accountant in Alberta, and I collect, buy and sell sports cards. I've set up at the Edmonton Sports Expo a handful of times — I'm not a full-time show vendor, but I've stood on both sides of the table.

I built this directory because I kept hitting the same problem myself: there was no single, current, genuinely national list of Canadian card shops. Searching turned up American directories, dead listings, and shops that closed years ago. The accounting side of my work also means I spend a fair amount of time on the money end of this hobby — what a collection is worth, what grading actually costs, what a dealer owes at tax time — which is where a lot of the guides here come from.

What's in the directory

614 card shops across 179 cities in 11 provinces and territories, plus 19 upcoming card shows with dates, venues and admission. 597 of the shops carry a public Google rating. It rebuilds every morning, so a shop that updates its hours or a show that confirms a date shows up here the next day rather than months later.

How listings are compiled

Listings come from public sources — a shop's own website and social pages, business directories, and submissions from readers — and a person reviews each one before it goes live. Generic sporting-goods stores, big-box retailers, and online-only sellers without a storefront are deliberately excluded: this is a directory of places you can actually walk into.

Ratings and review counts come from Google. Where a shop could not be matched confidently, its rating is left blank rather than guessed at — an empty field is honest, a wrong rating attached to a real business is not.

What "best" has to mean here

A shop is only described as best, top-rated, or a top pick if it has a Google rating backed by at least 20 reviews. 530 of the 614 listings currently clear that bar. Rankings use a weighted score rather than the raw average, so review volume counts as evidence — a shop rated 4.9 from hundreds of reviews ranks above one sitting at 5.0 from twenty. Shops below the bar are still listed and still findable; they just don't get crowned.

Independence

Nothing here is paid placement. No shop has paid to be listed, to rank higher, or to be described as best, and there is no arrangement under which they could. I run other card-hobby projects, which are linked in the footer and labelled as mine — none of them affect how shops are ranked on this site.

Corrections

If a listing here is wrong — a shop has moved, closed, changed hands, or should never have been listed — tell me and I'll fix it. Email slabsavvycpa@gmail.com, or use the suggest-a-store form. Corrections go live at the next daily rebuild. Shop owners can also ask to have their listing removed entirely, no reason required.

Common questions

Who runs Sports Cards Near Me?
Nathan Wiebe, a Chartered Professional Accountant in Alberta who collects, buys and sells sports cards. The directory is independent and not owned by a shop, a grader, or a marketplace.
Where do the listings come from?
Public sources — shops' own websites and social pages, business directories, and reader submissions — compiled and then checked by a person before publishing. The directory currently lists 614 shops and rebuilds every morning, so hours, listings and show dates stay current.
How do you decide which shop is "best"?
A shop is only called best, top-rated, or a top pick if it carries a Google rating backed by at least 20 reviews — 530 of our 614 listings currently clear that bar. Ranking uses a weighted score, so a shop with hundreds of reviews outranks one with a perfect score from a handful. Shops below the bar are still listed; they just are not crowned. See how a city ranking looks.
Can a shop pay to rank higher?
No. Nothing on this site is paid placement, and no shop has paid to appear or to rank. Rankings are computed from public Google ratings and review counts.
How do I get my shop or show listed, or fix a mistake?
Use the suggest-a-store or add-a-show forms — both are free and a person reviews every submission. For a correction to an existing listing, email slabsavvycpa@gmail.com and it will be fixed at the next daily rebuild. Suggest a store.

Know a shop or show we're missing? Suggest a store — it's free, and a person reviews every submission.
